subject.title: Feature Request: User-Level Skill Preferences/Conventions Support

question: Should OpenClaw support a markdown per-skill user preferences sidecar, and if so should it be a core skill-loader contract or a plugin/bundle convention?
rationale: The request changes skill loading precedence, prompt bytes, watcher invalidation, and session snapshot behavior, so automation should not choose the permanent user-facing contract.

options.title: Core markdown sidecar
options.body: Define `preferences.md` or `conventions.md` as a core loader contract with explicit precedence, versioning, watcher refresh, docs, and tests.

options.title: Plugin or bundle convention
options.body: Keep core unchanged and document how a skill or bundle can read its own adjacent preference file through existing skill instructions.

options.title: Structured config only
options.body: Decline markdown sidecars and steer users to `skills.entries.<key>.config`, accepting that natural-language preferences remain less ergonomic.

recommendation.title: Core markdown sidecar
recommendation.body: Define `preferences.md` or `conventions.md` as a core loader contract with explicit precedence, versioning, watcher refresh, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Most relevant history for the current skill loader, Claude skill integration, and custom skill config bag points to this owner path.
